findings.governingReading: Shirou acknowledges Rin’s report, then says her presence was a great help.
findings.explanation: Sorry invents an apology and alters the opening beat of his gratitude.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの体も良くならないし
findings.governingReading: Rin says merely removing Saber’s armor did not improve her condition.
findings.explanation: Won’t get well turns the limited result of Rin’s immediate action into a prediction that Saber will not recover.

findings.highlight: She was the one that yelled at me
findings.evidenceJa: 混乱していた俺を怒鳴りつけてくれた
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese says that Rin’s presence helped, then moves directly to her reading Saber’s condition; the line about yelling at Shirou is commented out.
findings.explanation: The English restores deleted narration and adds a harsher interaction to Rin’s conduct during the crisis.

findings.highlight: I thought you went out looking for Shinji, and Saber was like that
findings.evidenceJa: 帰ってきたと思ったらセイバーがアレでしょう
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou went looking for Shinji and, when he returned, Saber was in that condition.
findings.explanation: I thought falsely makes the expedition uncertain and loses the return-then-discovery relation.

findings.highlight: She’s Tohsaka, so she should be able to tell that it was no ordinary matter
findings.evidenceJa: それがただ事ではなかったと感づいているんだろう
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese contains only Rin’s voiced reaction to Saber’s Noble Phantasm; the suggestive silence and Shirou’s inference are commented out.
findings.explanation: The English restores deleted narration and gives Rin an unsupported moment of silent deduction.

findings.evidenceJa: 確かに、セイバーから言われた事だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou recognizes that Saber did indeed tell him this.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the recognition as a sentence fragment, weakening the clean confirmation.

findings.highlight: Phantasm that put her in this state to begin with.
findings.evidenceJa: 宝具を使うなんてもってのほか
findings.governingReading: Using the Noble Phantasm is out of the question; using it once more will certainly make Saber disappear.
findings.explanation: The English inserts a duplicated, ungrammatical fragment that is absent from the Japanese and disrupts the warning.

findings.highlight: ways to heal a Servant who ran out of magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーを以前の状態に戻す方法
findings.governingReading: Rin gives two ways to return Saber to her former condition.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes Saber’s case into healing any fully depleted Servant, although Saber still has some energy and the issue is sustained existence and combat capacity.

findings.highlight: That’ssomething I would have done already
findings.evidenceJa: それは出来るならとっくにそうしてるさ
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he would already have supplied energy if he knew how.
findings.explanation: The missing space visibly corrupts the sentence.

findings.evidenceJa: ぶつぶつと考え込む遠坂
findings.governingReading: Page 27 contains only commented-out narration; there is no displayed deliberation or emotionally suppressed stare.
findings.explanation: The English restores the entire deleted beat, making Rin visibly calculate and suppress emotion before proposing human sacrifice.

findings.highlight: her limit is still near.” near.
findings.evidenceJa: 限界は近いでしょうね
findings.governingReading: Rin says Saber’s limit is near despite sleep calming her.
findings.explanation: Near is duplicated outside the quotation, visibly corrupting the transition.

findings.highlight: If you’re going to make a decision, make one by the next time we get attacked.
findings.evidenceJa: 次に襲われるまでにね
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese leaves the decision to Shirou and says only that Saber’s limit is near; the next-attack deadline is commented out.
findings.explanation: The English restores a deleted deadline and materially increases Rin’s pressure with a specific cutoff.
